issues.legal_issue: A recovery provision that directs collection of certified tax arrears as land revenue and gives the collector civil-court powers does not confer alternative recovery procedures or unguided discretion to discriminate between similarly situated defaulters.
material_facts: A tax authority certified unpaid assessed tax for recovery by the collector.
The challenged provision directed the collector to recover the certified amount as if it were an arrear of land revenue and, in a proviso, gave the collector civil-court powers for that recovery.
The petitioner argued that the main provision and proviso supplied two alternative procedures that the collector could choose between at will.
issues.conclusion: The provision prescribed one recovery procedure: the applicable procedure for recovering land revenue. The proviso conferred additional powers to make that procedure more effective, not an alternative procedure, so this asserted basis for an equality violation failed.
issues.legal_principle: Article 14 forbids arbitrary discrimination, but the provision must be read as a whole. The court interpreted the main clause as prescribing recovery through the relevant land-revenue procedure and the proviso as adding powers to that procedure. It rejected the contrary reading in Shaik Ali Ahmed v. Collector of Bombay.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_tax_recovery: A person challenges the constitutionality of a process used to recover unpaid tax.
predicates.recovery_clause_specifies_one_land_reven: The governing clause directs the collector to use the procedure for recovering land revenue.
predicates.proviso_adds_enforcement_powers: A proviso gives the collector additional powers to carry out the recovery process rather than specifying a separate process.

issues.definition: When a tax-recovery challenge concerns a clause prescribing one land-revenue process and a proviso that only adds enforcement powers, the claim that the collector may choose arbitrarily between alternative processes is rejected.

issues.legal_issue: Applying different state-level land-revenue recovery procedures to tax defaulters according to the state in which they are situated is a permissible territorial classification when it is connected to the purpose of recovering public demands.
material_facts: The tax authority could seek recovery of unpaid tax from defaulters in different states.
The states had adopted different procedures for recovering their own land-revenue demands, including different rules on arrest and detention.
The challenged provision made those locally applicable procedures available for recovery of certified tax arrears.
The petitioner argued that tax defaulters were treated differently across states despite the tax being a union demand.
issues.conclusion: The statewise differences did not violate Article 14. The territorial classification was based on an intelligible differentia and had a reasonable nexus to the recovery purpose; the fact that the tax was a union demand did not change that result.
issues.legal_principle: Article 14 permits reasonable classification if it rests on an intelligible differentia and that differentia has a rational relation to the statute’s object; the rule applies to procedural as well as substantive laws. The court relied on Chiranjit Lal Chowdhury v. Union of India and Budhan Choudhry v. State of Bihar for the classification test, and on Middleton v. Texas Power and Light Company and Bowman v. Lewis in considering territorial classification. It distinguished State of Rajasthan v. Rao Manohar Singhji, where the challenged classification imposed disabilities on a particular group without evidence of a relevant difference. The court treated the locally devised recovery procedures as connected to local needs and to the closely related purpose of recovering public demands.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_tax_recovery: A person challenges the constitutionality of a process used to recover unpaid tax.
predicates.tax_defaulters_grouped_by_state: Tax defaulters are subjected to recovery procedures according to the state in which they are situated.
predicates.states_have_locally_devised_public_deman: States have developed procedures suited to their own needs for recovering public demands.
predicates.local_recovery_procedures_are_connected_: The locally applicable procedures are used to achieve the related purpose of recovering public demands.

issues.definition: When tax defaulters are grouped by state and locally devised recovery procedures are connected to recovery of public demands, statewise procedural differences do not defeat equal protection.

issues.legal_issue: Detention to recover unpaid tax does not violate personal liberty when it is carried out under valid laws that establish the procedure for the detention.
material_facts: A collector issued an arrest warrant under a land-revenue law to recover unpaid tax certified for collection under the tax statute.
The petitioner challenged the resulting arrest and detention as inconsistent with the constitutional guarantee of personal liberty.
The court upheld the challenged tax-recovery provision and found that the applicable land-revenue provision supplied the procedure for arrest and detention.
issues.conclusion: There was no violation of Article 21 because the arrest and detention were carried out under laws that constituted a procedure established by law.
issues.legal_principle: Article 21 prohibits deprivation of personal liberty except in accordance with procedure established by law. The court held that where the applicable statutory recovery provisions stand, and provide the procedure under which arrest and detention occur, the resulting detention does not infringe Article 21. The court considered the validity of the provisions under Article 14 before rejecting the Article 21 challenge.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_tax_recovery: A person challenges detention carried out to recover unpaid tax.
predicates.detention_carried_out_under_valid_recove: The detention is carried out under recovery laws that the court finds valid and that establish a procedure for detention.

issues.definition: When a person challenges tax-recovery detention and valid recovery laws establish the procedure used, the detention is not a violation of personal liberty.

issues.legal_issue: An arrest under an amended recovery provision is not invalid on the ground that the earlier version imposed a harsher procedure than the procedure applicable in other areas when the amendment removed that disparity before the arrest.
material_facts: The earlier city recovery provision allowed detention for a period that could be longer than the period allowed under the procedure applicable elsewhere in the state.
The provision was amended to impose a detention limit similar to the one applicable elsewhere in the state.
The property sale did not satisfy the certified tax demand, and the arrest warrant was issued after the amendment took effect.
The petitioner argued that the earlier version governed because the assessment, recovery certificate, demand notice, and attachment had preceded the amendment.
issues.conclusion: The arrest was governed by the amended provision because it was issued after the amendment and the need for arrest arose only after the sale proceeds proved insufficient. The amendment removed the disparity, so the provision as it then stood could not be assailed on that equality ground.
issues.legal_principle: Article 13(1) prevents an inconsistent law from obstructing the enjoyment of a fundamental right but does not obliterate that law from the statute book for all times or purposes. Relying on Bhikaji Narayan Dhakras v. State of Madhya Pradesh, the court held that an amendment can remove the relevant constitutional vice. The court did not decide whether the earlier provision was unconstitutional; it assumed that possibility for the purpose of deciding the challenge to the amended provision.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_tax_recovery: A person challenges an arrest carried out to recover unpaid tax.
predicates.recovery_provision_amended_before_arrest: The governing recovery provision was amended before the arrest occurred.
predicates.amendment_removed_relevant_procedural_di: The amendment brought the applicable recovery procedure into line with the relevant procedure used elsewhere.
predicates.arrest_became_necessary_after_recovery_s: The recovery sale left an unpaid balance, making arrest a later step in the recovery process.

issues.definition: When a recovery provision is amended to remove a procedural disparity before arrest, and arrest becomes necessary after a recovery sale, the arrest is not invalid merely because the earlier procedure differed.
